Article Title: Mizoram's 'misogynistic' marriage, divorce law faces challenge in SC
Article Text:
Mizo woman challenges marriage law in SC, calls it ‘misogynistic and pro-Mizo men’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Entrepreneur and Congress functionary Meriam L Hrangchal Monday challenged the constitutional validity of Mizo Marriage, Divorce and Inheritance of Property Act, 2014, which was enacted by Congress govt headed by Lal Thanhawla, terming it "misogynistic and pro-Mizo men".Hrangchal, daughter of former deputy CM Lalhmingthanga, told a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant that the law, which codified customary law, applied to any person belonging to a Mizo tribe and extended to marriages where the male member belonged to a Mizo tribe.The 2014 Act denies Mizo women, who marry outside the Mizo community, access to a comprehensive community-specific statutory framework governing marriage, property and inheritance, thereby infringing their right to equality, dignity and personal liberty under Articles 14 and 21, she said.The law marginalises the independent identity of Mizo women and refuses them the benefits under the 2014 Act which extends to marriage between a Mizo man and a non-Mizo woman but does not cover marriage between a Mizo woman and a non-Mizo man, she said, citing her own marital relationship."The effect of such provisions is that Mizo women who marry non-Mizo men, and the children born out of such marriages, are excluded from the statutory regime, notwithstanding their subsisting connection to the Mizo community," she said.The bench said the issue raised in her petition was important but asked why she was bypassing the high court. Her counsel said the community being small, she feared for her safety if her petition was heard by the Aizawl bench of Gauhati HC.The CJI-led bench understood her apprehension and requested the CJ of Gauhati HC to hear her petition in Guwahati without sending it to the Aizawl bench.
Article Summary: Mizo woman challenges marriage law in sc, calls it ‘misogynistic and pro-mizo men’ meriam l hrangchal monday challenged the constitutional validity of mizo marriage, divorce and inheritance of property act, 2014. The 2014 act denies mizo women access to a comprehensive community-specific statutory framework, she said.

Article Title: 22 million hectares of degraded land restored during 2011 and 2020
Article Text:
India restores nearly 22 million hectares of degraded land, says Bhupender Yadav at UN conference

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has restored nearly 22 million hectares of degraded and deforested land during the 2011-20 period as against its target of restoring 26 million hectares by 2030, said Union minister Bhupender Yadav at a UN conference Monday.While addressing the 17th session (COP17) of the UNCCD conference in Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, he also pitched for "diversified, adequate, predictable and sustained international finance" for land restoration and drought resilience, saying it is not a cost, but an investment in food, water, biodiversity, livelihood and long-term resilience.Underlining how the country's restoration efforts had generated approximately 1.2 billion person-days of employment during the 2011-20 period, he said these figures demonstrated restoration could deliver both environmental and socio-economic outcomes by reviving degraded landscapes while creating employment and supporting rural livelihoods.According to India’s second progress report on its land restoration efforts, covering the period 2011–2020, Telangana restored the maximum (4.2 million hectares) degraded area followed by Madhya Pradesh (3.8 million ha), Odisha (2.6 million ha), Gujarat (1.7 million ha) and Andhra Pradesh (1.6 million ha) through afforestation, water resource management, sustainable farming practices, agroforestry, mangrove restoration and natural regeneration of formerly forested land.India’s Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas shows that 97.8 million ha of land, or nearly 29.8% of the country’s geographical area, are affected by land degradation and desertification. Around 82% of India’s degraded land falls in nine states/UT - Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.Highlighting India’s innovative and diversified financing architecture for land restoration and drought resilience, Yadav noted the ‘Sovereign Green Bonds’ as an avenue to mobilise capital and underlined the country’s ‘Green Credit Programme’, which enables public and private entities to finance restoration of degraded forest land.Though the minister during his address flagged India’s experience demonstrating what the committed domestic resources can achieve, he stressed that this cannot substitute for “additional, adequate and predictable international finance” for restoration and drought resilience.
Article Summary: India restores nearly 22 million hectares of degraded land, says bhupender yadav at un conference. Yadav also pitched for "diversified, adequate, predictable and sustained international finance" for land restoration and drought resilience.

Article Title: Amit Shah focuses on new doctrine to fight terror & radicalisation
Article Text:
Amit Shah calls for stronger counter-terror training, faster trials and action against foreign-based masterminds

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah Monday emphasised enhanced training for implementing the country's first-ever counter-terrorism and counter-radicalisation doctrine, Prahaar, and expediting trial in cases with cross-border linkages by bringing back fugitives and using trial in absentia to bring foreign-based masterminds to justice.In his inaugural address at the two-day National Security Strategies Conference, being attended by over 850 officials from the security forces, agencies and police forces, Shah directed that an artificial intelligence-based analysis of information available on multi-agency centre (MAC) platforms be done to create standard operating procedures to counter various security challenges.The Union minister instructed all the agencies to take strict measures against infiltration and asked police forces to adopt a comprehensive and integrated approach while investigating Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act cases.The first day of the conference focused on discussing critical aspects of national security, including response to counter-terrorism challenges; fusion, analysis and operationalisation of intelligence through MAC; vision document on narcotics control; detection and deportation of illegal migrants; a policy framework to combat cyber-crime; and proxy warfare by Pakistan.On Tuesday, the conference will deliberate on the threat landscape from sub-aerial systems and formulating countermeasures, securing the blue economy, information warfare and its implications on national security, and the need for a bio-security framework.Prior to inaugurating the conference, the home minister paid tribute at the martyrs' column here, honouring the supreme sacrifice of Intelligence Bureau personnel to safeguard national security and integrity.The conference, being held in hybrid format, was attended by junior home ministers, deputy NSAs, heads of central paramilitary forces, DGPs of states and UTs, young cops working at the cutting-edge level and experts from specialised fields.
Article Summary: Amit shah calls for stronger counter-terror training, faster trials and action against foreign-based masterminds. Shah directed that an artificial intelligence-based analysis of information available on multi-agency centre (mac) platforms be done to create standard operating procedures to counter various security challenges.

Article Title: SC to consider Tarun Tejpal's plea for exemption from surrender
Article Text:
SC to decide on Tejpal’s plea against surrender after 10-year rape conviction

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday said it would pass order on former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal 's plea seeking exemption from surrender after Bombay High Court convicted and sentenced him to 10 years of imprisonment in a 2013 rape case, with Goa govt opposing his plea and contending that his appeal was not admissible since the convict had not filed a separate application seeking exemption from surrender or shown a certificate that he has already surrendered as per Order XXII Rule 5 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013.The matter was heard by a single judge, Justice Alok Aradhe. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state govt, contended that existence of the appeal was dependent on Tejpal either filing a certificate that he has surrendered or, alternatively, requesting the court to allow an exemption from surrender.Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, representing Tejpal, said there was no need to surrender yet since the high court itself had granted him time to surrender. "This rule doesn't apply because this is a case where stay has been granted by the high court, so there is no question of applying this rule. Suppose the court says no stay, I will have to go to jail," Sibal said, requesting the court to list the appeal for Aug 31.After hearing both sides, Justice Aradhe said he would pass an appropriate order in the matter.The Goa bench of Bombay high court convicted Tejpal under multiple provisions of the IPC and sentenced him to 10 years rigorous imprisonment each under sections 376(2)(f) and 376(2)(k), with the sentences to run concurrently. It also imposed additional concurrent sentences for offences relating to outraging a woman's modesty, sexual harassment, disrobing, wrongful restraint and wrongful confinement. The fines imposed on Tejpal total Rs 10.1 lakh, which the court directed to be paid to the victim. tnn
Article Summary: Sc to decide on tejpal’s plea against surrender after 10-year rape conviction. Goa govt opposing his plea and contending that his appeal was not admissible since the convict had not filed a separate application seeking exemption from surrender. The matter was heard by a single judge, justice alok aradhe.

Article Title: 3 Bambiha members deported from Malaysia
Article Text:
Three Bambiha gang operatives deported from Malaysia in major crackdown, says Amit Shah

NEW DELHI: In a major operation against the Bambiha criminal network, Indian agencies have executed a coordinated crackdown on its key overseas operatives, deporting three of its members from Malaysia who were ordering hits and carrying out extortions in India on behalf of the group's kingpin Lucky Patial.Announced by Union home minister Amit Shah on X Monday, the high-profile action targeted Jaspreet Singh (alias Jas Behbal) of Faridkot, alongside Ajay Singh (alias Ajay Malaysia) and Pawandeep Singh, both from Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district. Shah posted that Indian agencies had got the three absconding gangsters apprehended in Malaysia and deported to India."The fugitives....are linked to the Bambiha gang and are accused of multiple crimes, including extortion, cross-border arms and narco-trafficking, and a foiled grenade attack in Ludhiana...our agencies have facilitated the deportation of 51 hardened criminals in 2026 alone."
Article Summary: Three bambiha gang operatives deported from malaysia in major crackdown, says amit shah. High-profile action targeted jaspreet singh of faridkot, ajay singh and pawandeep singh. The fugitives are accused of multiple crimes, including extortion and cross-border arms.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday stepped up his attack on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on the Manusmriti, while also targeting the party's state leadership over its alleged conduct in Ayodhya.Speaking in Raebareli, CM Yogi said Rahul Gandhi, as leader of opposition, had a responsibility to uphold the Constitution and respect India's traditions and heritage.“Recently, I was reading a statement made by the Member of Parliament from Raebareli, Rahul Gandhi. He made a statement in Maharashtra urging women to break free from the shackles of the Manusmriti. Rahul ji, the country does not have high expectations of you merely as Rahul Gandhi; in fact, it has no expectations at all. However, your role as the Leader of the Opposition in Parliament entails accountability towards the country's democracy. You took an oath to uphold the Constitution of India, yet you seem to consider it your birthright to disparage India's traditions and heritage.”CM Yogi accused Gandhi of insulting Uttar Pradesh and India during visits outside the state and abroad. He also alleged that the Congress had questioned the existence of Lord Ram in Ayodhya and referred to the Emergency imposed in 1975.The UP chief minister said Rahul Gandhi should study ancient Indian texts to understand Manu and India's heritage.“You make comments regarding Manu, Ram, or India's heritage. If you wish to understand Manu, read the Atharvaveda, the Shatapatha Brahmana and the Matsya Purana; you will find all the information there.”Yogi also criticised remarks directed at the Prime Minister, saying such statements amounted to an attack on an institution rather than an individual.“When you insult India's institutions, when you make derogatory remarks about the Prime Minister of India, you are not merely insulting an individual; you are insulting an institution of India. The Prime Minister is not just an individual; the Prime Minister is an institution of India.”He added that such criticism could undermine public confidence in constitutional institutions and urged Gandhi to refrain from what he called irresponsible behaviour.CM Yogi also attacked the Congress state president over an alleged incident involving a visit to Hanumangarhi in Ayodhya, accusing him of displaying duplicity.“You saw the behaviour of the Congress state president: he goes to offer prayers at Hanumangarhi, but later outside he enjoys a feast of fish. He could have eaten whatever he wanted outside—anywhere other than Ayodhya. Yet, this is the duplicity they display. Even a chameleon would be put to shame by these people; it would wonder what kind of human species this is—chanting 'Ram-Ram' inside the temple and feasting on fish the moment they step out. This is their history—the history of this Congress state president.”CM Yogi further alleged that the Congress leader had bowed before a mafia figure who had allegedly killed his brother, claiming the situation changed only after the government acted against the accused.“When a mafia don murdered his brother, this man did not testify against the criminal; instead, he knelt and bowed in submission before him. He knelt before the very man who had brutally killed his brother. It was only when the government stepped in and crushed that mafia element that the situation changed; otherwise, these people had turned the state into a mafia-dominated territory, creating an identity crisis.”CM Yogi also said society could have no future if it forgot its ancestors and accused unnamed groups of attempting to weaken India's traditions, values and ideals.
Article Summary: Cm yogi slams rahul over manusmriti remarks. Cm yogi targets congress state leadership over its alleged conduct in ayodhya. Uttar pradesh chief minister said rahul gandhi should study ancient indian texts to understand manu and india's heritage.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday announced a set of welfare measures in the state Assembly, including three free cooking gas cylinders a year for eligible beneficiaries and an expansion of the fare-free bus travel scheme for women.Under the cooking gas scheme, the amount for the three cylinders will be credited directly to the bank accounts of eligible beneficiaries.Vijay announced the launch of the Vetri Payanam scheme, expanding the existing fare-free bus travel programme for women across the state.Under the scheme, women will be allowed to travel free of charge on Express, LSS and Deluxe government buses operating in metropolitan and urban areas. NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra has approached the Supreme Court alleging that the Nadia district administration in West Bengal evicted her from her official constituency accommodation at the Circuit House in violation of court orders.The matter was mentioned before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, seeking urgent listing of Moitra’s plea.Moitra told the Supreme Court that local officials evicted her from her constituency accommodation in the middle of the night despite a protective order issued by the high court, as cited by Bar and Bench."May I mention an Article 32 petition by a sitting lady member of parliament who was evicted from her constituency accommodation by local officials, the Additional District Magistrate and the District Magistrate, in the dead of the night at 11 pm. Article Title: Parandur airport project dropped: CM Vijay backs farmers, DMK warns of economic damage
Article Text:
The Tamil Nadu government has abandoned the Parandur greenfield airport project

(With agency inputs)





CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu government has decided to abandon steps to establish the proposed greenfield airport at Parandur, chief minister C Joseph Vijay announced in the Assembly on Monday, saying the project would affect agricultural land and disrupt the livelihoods of farmers and residents.Vijay said Chennai needs a new airport because of rising passenger traffic, industrial development and increasing cargo movement. However, he said the new airport should be located at a site where agricultural land and residential areas are minimally affected.Speaking in the Assembly, Vijay said Chennai's Meenambakkam airport, operated by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), currently has the capacity to handle around 30 million passengers annually. With Terminal 3 becoming operational, the capacity is expected to rise to 34 million passengers per year, he said.The government is also planning to construct a fifth terminal on the northwestern side of the existing airport, which Vijay said would add another 20 million passengers annually.Vijay said he had visited Eganapuram and other villages on January 20, 2025, and heard the grievances of residents protesting against the Parandur airport project."I stand firmly with the people protesting against the airport to be established in Chennai's Parandur and 12 surrounding villages," he said.Calling farmers the backbone of the country, Vijay said the government would not allow an airport project that disrupted agricultural land and people's livelihoods.He said he had opposed the Parandur project at a public meeting in Vikravandi in October 2024, while maintaining that he supported industrial development and the role of airports in promoting it."However, this project should not be located in Parandur. The government must reconsider this project," Vijay said, adding that an alternative site should be identified where minimum agricultural land was affected and people's livelihoods were not disrupted.Vijay said consultations had been held with senior officials and experts on the proposed airport."To fulfill the promise I made to the people that day... the steps taken to establish a new airport in Parandur will be abandoned by this government," he said.The chief minister said new sites were being considered and the location would be finalised soon after a technical feasibility study by expert teams.He also accused the previous DMK government of selecting a site that would require the relocation of a large number of people and affect agricultural land.The Civil Aviation Ministry had granted in-principle approval in April 2025 for setting up an international greenfield airport at Parandur in Kancheepuram district.The announcement drew sharp criticism from the opposition DMK.Former Tamil Nadu minister and DMK MLA Thangam Thennarasu said scrapping the project for political reasons would cause economic damage to the state and could prompt industries to move to neighbouring Andhra Pradesh."Possibilities for setting up two runways were all studied and only then Parandur was selected," Thennarasu told reporters.He said former chief minister MK Stalin had stated that the Parandur airport project would be dropped, but the state government had not conveyed any such decision to the Centre.Thennarasu also said compensation had already been provided to people whose land was acquired for the project."As per the Land Acquisition Act, the land acquired should be used only for the purpose for which it was acquired," he said.He maintained that Parandur was the best location for the proposed airport and warned that abandoning the project could have wider economic consequences."It would be best to have the airport at Parandur. Dropping the Parandur Airport project for political reasons will cause economic damage," Thennarasu said.He also warned that several industries could shift to Andhra Pradesh if the project was scrapped."Many industries will move towards Andhra Pradesh. We have already lost the Hosur Airport," he said.The DMK also staged a walkout from the Assembly, protesting against being denied an opportunity to speak in the House on the Parandur airport issue.The Vijay government's decision means the state will now have to identify an alternative location for Chennai's proposed second airport while expanding capacity at the existing Meenambakkam facility.
Article Summary: The tamil nadu government has abandoned steps to establish the proposed greenfield airport at parandur. Chief minister c joseph vijay said the project would affect agricultural land and disrupt the livelihoods of farmers and residents. The announcement drew sharp criticism from the opposition dmk.

NEW DELHI: Heavy rain lashed Delhi-NCR on Monday, causing widespread waterlogging, traffic snarls and flight disruptions, with 15 Delhi-bound flights diverted.Fifteen flights Delhi-bound flights diverted, including two international flights, with 11 diverted to Jaipur. Passengers have been advised to check with their respective airlines for the latest flight updates.The weather office issued red and orange alerts for heavy to moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and winds of up to 40 kmph.Heavy rain and thunderstorms were witnessed at isolated places in South East Delhi, East Delhi, Shahdara, Central Delhi, North East Delhi, South Delhi, New Delhi, South West Delhi, West Delhi, North West Delhi and North Delhi.Between 8.30am and 11.30am, Chhatarpur recorded the highest rainfall in Delhi at 28mm, followed by Lodi Road at 24.6mm and Pitampura at 18.5mm, according to the IMD.The Ridge recorded 5mm of rainfall, Mayur Vihar 1.5mm, Safdarjung 1mm and Ayanagar 0.1mm during the period.The showers were accompanied by strong winds in several areas, with waterlogging reported around New Ashok Nagar Metro Station, Burari, C R Park and Alaknanda.Commuters took to social media to share visuals of waterlogged roads and traffic disruptions. Commuters were seen wading through the flooded Zakhira underpass, while rainwater accumulated in a parking lot at Connaught Place.Students navigated severely waterlogged streets in Sangam Vihar, and children were seen swimming and playing on inundated roads in Durga Vihar.Waterlogging was also reported from Gurugram's Sector 46 and several locations in Noida, including Sector 95.Delhi recorded a minimum temperature of 27.8 degrees Celsius at Safdarjung on Monday, 1.4 degrees above normal. The Ridge recorded the lowest minimum temperature in the city at 24 degrees Celsius.Air India advised passengers travelling to and from Delhi to check their flight status before heading to the airport, warning that adverse weather could impact flight operations.IndiGo also issued a travel advisory, saying bad weather over Delhi had affected flight schedules. The airline urged passengers to check their flight status on its website or app before leaving for the airport and advised them to allow additional travel time as road conditions could be slower than usual.(With Agency Inputs)
Article Summary: Weather office has issued red and orange alerts for heavy to moderate rainfall. Chhatarpur recorded the highest rainfall in delhi at 28mm, followed by lodi road at 24.6mm and pitampura at 18.5mm. Air india advised passengers travelling to and from delhi to check their flight status.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced a youth march on September 5 in Delhi, accusing the government of failing to honour commitments that led to the withdrawal of the students’ protest at Jantar Mantar on July 25. The CJP said the government had failed to act on its assurance to withdraw FIRs against students and protesting students.The march will begin at India Gate and proceed towards the New Delhi Police Headquarters, according to a statement issued by the CJP National Working Committee, posted on X. The organisation said the protest would be led by families of deceased NEET victims and victims of alleged police brutality, with students and youth organisations expected to join.In the post, the CJP said, “The Cockroach Janta Party strongly condemns the Union Government’s failure to honour the commitments made to India’s youth on July 25, particularly those concerning the withdrawal of FIRs against students and protesters.”“With the Government continuing to delay and avoid fulfilling its assurances, the CJP National Working Committee has decided to resume peaceful mobilisation,” it said.The CJP said the decision followed a review of the commitments it alleges were made by the government on July 25, after which nationwide youth protests were withdrawn.The statement said the committee had expressed “serious doubts over whether the Government intends to honour its word at all”, alleging that the government had delayed action and avoided providing clear commitments.It also referred to proceedings before the Supreme Court, saying that on August 18, the court had sought a list of FIRs registered across the country so that it could consider dealing with them together. The CJP alleged that the government had not given a clear commitment on the issue.The organisation also added, “This cannot continue. Our patience cannot be mistaken for weakness. Our good faith cannot become an opportunity for the Government to betray us.”Announcing the September 5 mobilisation, the CJP said, “We announce a peaceful protest march from India Gate to the new Delhi Police Headquarters on 5 September, led by the families of the deceased NEET victims and victims of police brutality, and joined by students and young citizens from across the country.”The group said it had returned to the streets because the government “appears determined to commit a ‘vishwasghaat’ with Gen-Z, the young generation of this country, and the families who have already lost their children.”It further said, “We withdrew a nationwide movement in good faith. A government cannot take the trust of an entire generation, use it to send them home, and then quietly retreat from its own word. We will not accept this attempted betrayal.”The CJP has urged students, youth organisations and young citizens to gather at India Gate on September 5. “The families who lost their children will walk at the front. Victims of police brutality will walk with them,” the statement said.Earlier, the CJP, that describes itself as a youth-focused movement, had led a 37-day protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, alongside activist Sonam Wangchuk’s 26-day hunger strike.On July 25, following talks with Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh, the CJP said the government had accepted its demands, including suitable compensation for families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide and withdrawal of FIRs against protesters. “All our demands have been accepted, so we request the protesters to withdraw immediately and return home peacefully,” it said.The Supreme Court later directed states to release eligible students detained during the protests and barred coercive action against students for the time being.
Article Summary: The cockroach janta party (cjp) has announced a youth march on september 5 in delhi. The march will begin at india gate and proceed towards the new delhi police headquarters. The organisation said the protest would be led by families of deceased neet victims and victims of alleged police brutality.

Article Title: 'Hindu baiter': CM Himanta slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti row

NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Monday joined the escalating political row over Rahul Gandhi ’s remarks on the Manusmriti, accusing the Congress leader of using women’s rights as a 'smokescreen' to target Hinduism and challenging him to support a Uniform Civil Code (UCC).Sarma, in a post on X, said, “Rahul Gandhi is NO champion of women’s rights. He is simply a Hindu baiter, using the cause of women’s empowerment as a convenient smokescreen to target and discredit Hindu Dharma.”The Assam chief minister’s remarks came after Gandhi, during an interaction with girl students in Pune on Saturday, criticised what he called a “Manusmriti mindset” and urged women to “smash patriarchy”.Sarma questioned Gandhi’s position by asking, “Consider this: how many times has he spoken with the same outrage against patriarchal and medieval practices that persist under Sharia? NEVER.”He further argued that Manusmriti and Sharia should not be treated as equivalent sources of authority, writing, “While Sharia is foundational to Islamic jurisprudence, Manusmriti has no comparable scriptural authority in Hindu Dharma. It is not even a universally binding code for Hindus.”Sarma then directly challenged the Congress leader over the issue of a common civil law. “So here is a simple challenge to Rahul Gandhi: If women’s equality truly comes before politics, will he unequivocally support a Uniform Civil Code that guarantees equal rights irrespective of religion?” he said.Sarma also alleged that Congress had a record of compromising on women’s rights, referring to the Shah Bano case and the Triple Talaq legislation. He further claimed that Gandhi had ensured that no woman was included in the Karnataka state Cabinet.The remarks came after the LoP’s interaction with students, where he said women should not be defined solely through their relationships with men.Rahul said women belong to themselves and not to their fathers, husbands or sons, while describing as shameful the Manusmriti’s prescription that women remain under the authority of male relatives at different stages of their lives.Referring to a verse from the ancient text, Gandhi said, “These words are a shame. These words should not have been spoken.”The controversy has since widened, with Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis among other prominent BJP faces criticised Rahul’s remarks.CM Adityanath earlier questioned Gandhi’s role as Leader of Opposition and said, “Whether you accept the Manusmriti or not is your choice, but do not acquaint people with wrong facts.”

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court on Monday issued summons to commentator Abhijit Iyer-Mitra and several media platforms in a suit filed by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das , who has alleged that his residential address and other personal details were published on social media without his consent.The development came during the hearing of Das's plea seeking interim protection against the alleged disclosure of his personal information. The court was informed that X, formerly known as Twitter, had removed the posts allegedly carrying Das's residential address.Justice Sachin Datta issued notice on Das's application seeking interim relief and directed the defendants to file their replies. The matter will next be heard on September 14.Senior Advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for Das, submitted that personnel of The Pamphlet had entered his client's residential property without permission and recorded a video.Sibal alleged that Iyer-Mitra subsequently added to the video and shared it on social media. He further submitted that some posts on X specifically mentioned Das's residential address.Seeking protection for his client, Sibal urged the court to ensure that the posts, which had already been removed by X under its policy, were not restored.Appearing for X, counsel told the court that the concerned links were "no longer accessible." The submission was recorded by the court.Counsel for The Pamphlet also submitted that the posts were no longer available on X and sought time to respond to the allegations on merits.The court further allowed Das to correct the name of The Sunday Guardian in the proceedings and permitted him to amend the memo of parties and plaint within three days.Apart from Iyer-Mitra and The Pamphlet, the suit names LawBeat, The Jaipur Dialogues, The Sunday Guardian, Google LLC and X Corp as defendants.Das has sought permanent and mandatory injunctions against the defendants, besides damages, alleging violation of his privacy, dignity and security.In his plea, Das alleged that his residential address and other personal details were recorded and circulated without his consent. He claimed that the disclosure of his exact address could expose him and other occupants of his residence to security risks.Das further alleged that representatives of The Pamphlet entered the residential premises where he lives and recorded videos of the property, including its interiors, which were later posted on X.His plea also claimed that he had faced threats and targeted hostility in the past because of his journalistic work, public-interest disclosures and political activities.During the hearing, Das's counsel emphasised the potential security implications of making a person's residential details publicly available and sought continued protection against any restoration or further circulation of the allegedly offending posts.The court, however, has not yet adjudicated the allegations on the merits. The defendants have been given an opportunity to file their responses.The matter will next come up before the Delhi High Court on September 14.
Article Summary: Delhi hc summons iyer-mitra, media portals over alleged disclosure of saurav das's address. Court was informed that x, formerly known as twitter, had removed the posts allegedly carrying das's residential address. The matter will next come up before the delhi high court on september 14.

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress (TMC) general secretary and Lok Sabha MP Abhishek Banerjee has moved Supreme Court seeking an early decision by Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla on disqualification pleas against 20 rebel party MPs. The party has argued that such conduct attracts disqualification under the anti-defection provisions of the Constitution.The rebel MPs, however, have maintained that their move constitutes a valid merger.The petition names the Lok Sabha speaker and the house secretary general as respondents, besides the 20 MPs against whom the disqualification proceedings have been sought.The MPs named in the petition are Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachana Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Md Abu Taher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Khalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.The TMC has alleged that the rebel MPs have subsequently been treated as an NCPI group in Parliament and have participated in National Democratic Alliance (NDA) parliamentary activities.The case comes against the backdrop of a broader political realignment in West Bengal following the TMC’s defeat in the 2026 Assembly elections.Supreme Court is also hearing a separate petition by Shiv Sena (UBT) challenging the Speaker’s approval of the merger of six of its MPs with the Shiv Sena led by Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. Article Title: Flood-rescued elephant Joymoti airlifted and shifted to Anant Amabani’s Vantara for specialised care
Article Text:
Ensuring the highest standards of welfare during air transport

Joymoti’s story highlights the need for specialised veterinary care facilities closer to where wildlife emergencies occur

Joymoti, a 53-year-old female elephant rescued from the devastating floods in Nagaland and Assam in July, was airlifted and moved to Vantara, Jamnagar, where she has already begun receiving immediate and specialised veterinary treatment.The elephant was swept away by floodwaters in Nagaland during the second week of July and was subsequently rescued by local communities with the assistance of government agencies. She sustained multiple injuries during the incident, including wounds to her forehead, right ear, the area above her tail, left inner thigh and abdomen, as well as a deep, maggot-infested wound around her external genital area. Her right eye is severely damaged, leaving her blind in that eye, with persistent tearing. She also has longstanding lameness in her left hind leg, resulting from a fracture sustained during logging, which affects her ability to walk normally and access food and water.Following her rescue, Joymoti received first aid and primary veterinary care locally, including wound dressing, pain medication, multivitamin and mineral supplements and supportive treatment. However, given the severity and multiple locations of her injuries, her advancing age and existing mobility challenges, she requires immediate treatment in a specialised hospital setting.Joymoti's transfer to Vantara is solely for immediate and specialised veterinary treatment. The decision to airlift her has been taken with her welfare and medical needs at the centre, allowing her to reach a specialised elephant hospital while minimising the duration and physical demands of ground transportation. Upon arrival at Vantara, Joymoti will undergo a comprehensive veterinary assessment and receive specialised treatment for her injuries and eye condition, along with nutritional and supportive care as required.Transporting an elephant by air for specialised hospital care is an unusual undertaking in India, requiring extensive veterinary, animal-care and logistical planning. Joymoti's transfer is being planned and carried out with careful attention to her health, comfort and safety at every stage, from her veterinary assessment and preparation before travel to loading, monitoring during the flight and her arrival at the hospital.Air transport can significantly reduce the duration of a long-distance journey for an animal requiring urgent medical attention. For elephants with serious injuries, chronic health conditions or mobility challenges, reducing journey time and avoiding prolonged ground travel can be an important consideration in protecting their welfare.Joymoti’s case also highlights the importance of having specialised elephant veterinary care facilities closer to areas where elephants are affected by floods, human-wildlife conflict and other health emergencies.Vantara has proposed the establishment of three wildlife veterinary care centres in Assam, including a dedicated centre for elephants, to strengthen local capacity for wildlife emergency veterinary care. The proposed centres would include species-specific facilities and veterinary support, enabling animals in need to receive timely and appropriate treatment closer to where emergencies occur. The centres would be operated completely independently by the Assam Forest Department.The aim is to strengthen local capacity so that elephants and other wildlife in Assam can receive high-quality care closer to home, avoiding the need for long-distance transportation whenever specialised treatment is required.Joymoti’s journey to Vantara is not a permanent relocation, but an urgent medical transfer undertaken solely to provide the specialised lifesaving treatment she currently requires. Her case underscores the importance of strengthening local veterinary capacity while ensuring that animals requiring advanced care can access it safely and without delay. At Vantara, the immediate priority is to provide Joymoti with the specialised treatment she needs and the best possible chance of recovery and a healthy, safe and dignified life.
